items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Fletcher had a bass player was an original bass player named Ralph Escoderá.

ctx.x: (Inaudible). And it had a funny ring to it, but John could play it. John could play that thing. But I'll tell you a story on John Kirby. You know,

John was in New York, and the guys used to hang out. Fletcher had a bass player was an original bass player named Ralph Escoderá. After Ralph Escoderá, there was another bass player called Bobby Vs Iguirre, Father Segueiri. He was a foreign guy. He was an excellent bass player, reading wise, but he couldn't improvise, you know, one of those things, put those extra beats in, things like that.

Well, Hawk and three or four of the other guys, Jimmy Harrison, he knew John Kirby, and they had gone around to where John was playing with a small combo, and they came and told Fletcher about him. Man, you ought to put in a man named John Kirby, plays bass. He can play tuba, and, you know, he plays upright bass. So Fletcher says, 'Well, if you guys think he's good, I'll go listen to him,' so Fletcher did, and -- funny thing about it, John was a little reluctant to come in the band at that time because he was…
